newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close lower in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close lower in consolidation.

text.p: The French stockmarket finished lower on Thursday as the bourse pursued a consolidation for a second day on its strong recent gains.
"What everyone was expecting is happening -- an orderly consolidation. It's positive. It reminds people that the market doesn't only move in one direction," a trader said.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 19.52 points, or 0.75 percent, at 2,575.24 -- a solid support level -- after losing 0.87 percent on Wednesday. The CAC-40 February futures contract fell 27 points to 2,572.
Volume was a brisk 7.5 billion francs.
Traders said the market may ease further during the monthly settlement on Friday.
Credit Lyonnais certificates rallied against the trend, closing up 6.32 percent at 198.40 francs.

The newspaper Les Echos said the state-owned bank expects to report between 3.4 and 3.7 billion francs of net attributable profit for 1997 after a profit close to 300 million francs for 1996. Brokerage Dupont-Denant upgraded the share to market performer from underperformer.
